insights.insight: Crinkl has processed $4,927,520 in cryptographically verified purchase GMV across 93,816 receipts — the $5M milestone is less than $72,500 away at current weekly pace of $92–97K, making this a live proof-of-scale moment for a protocol built on deterministic purchase confirmation rather than probabilistic inference.

insights.topic: Grocery dominates verified spend; Walmart leads by a wide margin
insights.insight: Grocery-supermarkets accounts for 1,502 receipts and $67,510 in verified GMV over 14 days — the single largest category by both volume and spend — with Walmart at 358 receipts leading all brands, more than double the next grocery competitor; Kroger (148) is now closing on Costco (159) after a multi-snapshot widening trend reversed.

insights.topic: Receipt throughput is structurally steady at 340–370 per day
insights.insight: Complete UTC-day analysis confirms a consistent daily receipt intake with a repeatable evening acceleration window (T20:00–T00:15 UTC) that drives the highest single-interval counts; this is a structural pattern, not noise, giving planners a predictable data refresh cadence to build against.

insights.topic: QSR, home improvement, and regional grocery now represented
insights.insight: McDonald's (entered Oct 12), Lowe's (Oct 15), and H-E-B (Oct 16) have joined the verified brand set, extending coverage beyond national grocery into quick-service restaurants, home improvement, and Texas-dominant regional retail — though no new brand entries have appeared across eleven consecutive snapshots since Oct 16, suggesting the current beta user base has a defined geographic and behavioral footprint.

insights.topic: 17 active metro areas with one structural contraction
insights.insight: The protocol covers 30 category/metro cells across 17 metro areas; metro count dropped from 18 to 17 between Oct 20 and Oct 21 and has held at 17 across five consecutive snapshots — no longer reads as transient data dropout, and marketers targeting specific DMAs should treat current metro coverage as the operative boundary until evidence of reversal.

insights.topic: The probabilistic-to-deterministic pricing gap is the core buy
insights.insight: The industry standard CPM for probabilistic behavioral targeting runs above $5; each verified receipt here carries a ~$0.10 settlement value against confirmed real-world purchase behavior — the signal is deterministic, category-tagged, and brand-attributed, which is the data type cookieless targeting alternatives are attempting to reconstruct through inference at higher cost.
